No public signature, return value or control-flow change. validate_connection still returns False on the same exceptions, so callers (startup.validate_connections at startup.py:160, and the subclasses radarr.py, sonarr.py and lidarr.py that inherit it) are unaffected functionally.

Blast radius is operator-facing log output only. It covers every enabled *arr instance at every startup, plus any path that calls validate_connection. The output goes to stderr/Docker logs and to the in-memory log buffer the web UI renders (triggarr/logging.py:71-76).

Direction: this diff LOOSENS a control. The repo has a deliberate 'sanitization split' (engine.py:30-44 _sanitize_exc, applied at scheduler.py:221-228, scheduler.py:406-410, routes.py:957-971 and routes.py:1062-1076) under which httpx/pydantic exceptions are never str()-formatted into logs. Per the global CLAUDE.md precedence rule ('check how the same problem is solved elsewhere in the repo and follow that'), the diff introduces a different, less safe pattern for the same problem it is solved for elsewhere in this very file.

Did not verify whether `httpx.HTTPStatusError.__str__`/`pydantic.ValidationError.__str__` literally contain the API key byte-for-byte in this app's current httpx/pydantic versions — the finding rests on the rule text plus the repo's own documented prior security fix and its logging.py docstring ('e.g. httpx exception messages containing API keys'), which together establish this as a recognized, previously-mitigated risk in this exact codebase, not a theoretical one.
